name: Baton Rouge Arsenal
notes: U.S. arsenal and barracks seized by Louisiana 10 Jan 1861. On 16 Mar 1861 the War Department ordered 'Capt. J. C. Booth, Corps of Artillery, Commanding Baton Rouge Arsenal' to issue shot, shell and cartridges to Bragg. The date of transfer from Louisiana to the C.S. was not found. [established: needs-source]

name: Mount Vernon Arsenal
sources: OR I-1 p.327; OR IV-1 p.192; OR IV-1 p.209
notes: Seized by Alabama State troops 4 Jan 1861. On 6 Apr Walker told the Alabama A&IG that 'the order you request will be transmitted to Captain White, in command of the arsenal at Mount Vernon' (first name not given). Alabama recruits were held there. Whether White then held his command from the State or the C.S. is ambiguous (side set to confederate because the C.S. War Department sent him orders). [established: needs-source]

name: Provisional Forces, Charleston Harbor (Beauregard's command)
notes: The C.S. government took over control of military operations at Charleston on 1 Mar 1861 (Walker to Pickens). Beauregard was ordered there on 1 Mar and authorised to receive up to 5,000 men. He arrived on 3 Mar, and that day the South Carolina War Department (D. F. Jamison) ordered all State officers, volunteers, enlisted men and militia to obey him. His General Orders No. 1 (6 Mar) assumed command of all troops ('[Regulars?], Volunteers, and Militia', first word OCR unclear in both scans) in and near Charleston Harbor. On 20 Mar the command was extended to the South Carolina coast from Beaufort to Georgetown. Headquarters styled 'Provisional Army C.S.' / 'Provisional Forces'. Staff under GO 1: Capt. D. R. Jones AAG; Capt. Stephen D. Lee (S.C. regular artillery), acting AQMG and ACG; Capt. S. W. Ferguson (S.C. regular infantry), ADC; 1st Lt Joseph J. Legare, secretary. Requisitions: 9 Mar, 3,000 needed at Charleston (no governor named); 8 Apr, 3,000 volunteers asked of South Carolina, and Pickens replied on 11 Apr that one 12-company regiment would gather at Columbia and two more regiments would be held ready. GO 22 (15 Apr) made the Morris Island forces a division under Bonham. Most troops stayed South Carolina State forces in the window (see the st_ posts and force blocks).

name: Forces on Morris Island (sub-command of Charleston)
notes: A sub-command under Beauregard, held by South Carolina State officers. Col. Maxcy Gregg signs as 'Commander on Morris Island' on 8 Mar. GO 13 (11 Apr) assigned Brig. Gen. James Simons, and Maj. W. H. C. Whiting was made acting AAIG for the island. GO 22 (15 Apr) made the island's forces one division under Maj. Gen. M. L. Bonham, S.C.V., in two brigades: 1st, Simons (Cunningham's and Hagood's regiments, De Saussure's artillery battalion); 2nd, Brig. Gen. P. H. Nelson, S.C.V. (Gregg's and Kershaw's regiments, the battalion of Rion's regiment). Side: confederate as a command; its troops are State forces. [established: needs-source]

name: Fort Morgan (Mobile Point)
notes: Seized by Alabama State troops 5 Jan 1861 (with Fort Gaines). A 'Captain Jones, Fort Morgan' was copied on Walker's warning telegram of 14 Mar (first name not given). Col. W. J. Hardee, colonel of the 1st Infantry, C.S. Army, was addressed as 'Commanding Fort Morgan' on 23 Mar and wrote from the fort on 9 Apr. Requisition 9 Mar: 1,000 from Alabama for Fort Morgan. The Alabama A&IG (28 Mar) expected at least 400 of the State troops at the fort to agree to transfer. On 6 Apr he expected the volunteer companies 'to fill the contingent at Fort Morgan' to be organised within the week. Fort Gaines: no commander or strength found. [established: needs-source]

name: C.S. Navy guard steamers, Charleston Harbor
notes: Commander H. J. Hartstene, C.S. Navy, commanded the guard expedition of 6 Apr: Gordon (flag), Lady Davis (Lt Cmdg W. G. Dozier, C.S. Navy) and General Clinch. On 9-10 Apr he also had Charleston, Seabrook and Catawba, and he carried C.S. recruits from Castle Pinckney (25 men per steamer on three steamers). Naval officers ashore: Lt J. R. Hamilton (floating battery and Point Dahlgren); Lt T. B. Huger; Lt A. F. Warley (Dahlgren channel battery); Lt Rutledge (called 'South Carolina Navy' on 26 Mar; acting inspector-general of ordnance of batteries). Beauregard calls Hartstene one of his volunteer aides. [established: needs-source]

name: Pensacola Navy Yard (Warrington)
notes: U.S. yard surrendered 12 Jan 1861 to Florida forces. In January Capt. V. M. Randolph was 'in charge of the navy-yard for the State of Florida'. On 14 Mar the War Department placed the yard under Bragg ('convey this information to Captain Farrand'), so the parent post is Bragg's command. Capt. D. N. Ingraham wrote from the yard on 2 Apr, and Bragg referred to 'Commodore Ingraham ... at the navy yard' on 12 Apr. When the yard passed from Florida to C.S. control: needs-source. [established: needs-source] [parent cs_cmd_pensacola is not part of the 5 March start]

name: Secretary of War
sources: OR IV-1 p.106; OR IV-1 p.135; OR IV-1 p.147; OR IV-1 p.211; OR IV-1 pp.221-222; JCCS p.71; JCCS p.73
notes: Act to establish the War Department approved 21 Feb 1861. REQUISITIONS ON THE STATES: (1) 9 Mar 1861, under the act to raise provisional forces: needs stated as Charleston 3,000, Fort Pulaski 1,000, Fort Morgan 1,000, Pensacola 5,000, Mississippi River below New Orleans 700, Texas 1,000; quotas asked of governors: Alabama 1,000 for Fort Morgan and 1,000 for Pensacola; Florida 500 Pensacola; Georgia 1,000 Pensacola and 1,000 Fort Pulaski; Louisiana 1,000 Pensacola and 700 Forts Jackson and St. Philip; Mississippi 1,500 Pensacola (no governor named for the Charleston and Texas figures). (2) 8 Apr 1861, conditional call to raise and hold volunteers in instant readiness: 3,000 each from South Carolina, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Texas, Mississippi; 1,500 from Florida (total 19,500). (3) After the window, 16 Apr 1861: a further 5,000 each from Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas and 2,000 from Florida. Congress appropriated (act approved 11 Mar 1861) for 3,000 men at Charleston for twelve months plus 2,000 more if required.

(Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Saint Louis. Missouri is nonetheless credited with 10,591 men under the call (OR III-1 p.69). 17 Apr the Illinois governor's party reported the state militia and police at Saint Louis 'under the control of the secessionists' (OR III-1 p.80). No statement of his between 4 Mar and 15 Apr found in folder sources. Capital: Executive Department, Jefferson City (OR III-1 p.82).

name: Governor of New Hampshire
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.73; OR III-1 p.75; OR III-1 p.103
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: loyal. Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 1 regiment (37 officers, 743 men, 780 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Portsmouth. Answer: complied, 16 Apr 1861 ('will furnish the men required'). 16 Apr: rendezvous by 20 May suffices. Men furnished: 779. State adjutant general Joseph C. Abbott (OCR 'Joseph O. Abbott') writes from Concord 23 Apr (OR III-1 p.103). Capital: governor addressed at Concord (OR III-1 p.73, p.75).

name: Governor of New Jersey
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.73; OR III-1 p.83
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: loyal. Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 4 regiments plus 1 brigadier-general (151 officers, 2,972 men, 3,123 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Trenton. Answer: complied, 17 Apr 1861 (letter of the 15th received that morning; 'measures will be immediately taken to comply'). 16 Apr the state quartermaster-general Lewis Perrine asked, for the governor, whether the US would arm and equip the troops (OR III-1 p.73). Men furnished: 3,123. Capital: Executive Department, Trenton (OR III-1 p.83).

name: Governor of New York
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.72; OR III-1 p.83
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: loyal. Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 17 regiments plus 2 major-generals and 4 brigadier-generals (649 officers, 12,631 men, 13,280 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous New York, Albany, Elmira. Answer: complied. 15 Apr asked for details by telegraph, the Legislature might adjourn that night (indorsed: reply stating number of regiments); 17 Apr asked whether the US would uniform and equip the volunteers and offered regiments ready at New York. Men furnished: 13,906. State adjutant general: see st_adjutant_general_new_york. Capital: Albany (OR III-1 p.72).

name: Governor of North Carolina
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.63-66; OR III-1 p.72; OR IV-1 p.160
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: border (upper South). Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 2 regiments (74 officers, 1,486 men, 1,560 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Raleigh. Answer: refused, 15 Apr 1861 ('You can get no troops from North Carolina'; doubted the dispatch was genuine) (OR III-1 p.72). Stance in the window: 2 Apr his private secretary Graham Daves pressed the War Department for the state's 1861 arms quota in rifles (Cameron answered 12 Apr) (OR III-1 p.63-66); the Georgia commissioner received cordially at Raleigh on 11 Feb (report 13 Mar 1861, OR IV-1 p.160). Capital: Cameron addressed him at Raleigh (OR III-1 p.66).

name: Governor of Ohio
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.73; OR III-1 p.77
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: loyal. Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 13 regiments plus 1 major-general and 3 brigadier-generals (494 officers, 9,659 men, 10,153 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Columbus, Cleveland. Answer: complied, 15 Apr 1861 ('will be promptly responded to'; earlier that day he asked the President what portion was Ohio's, indorsed 'Thirteen regiments'); 16 Apr two regiments could move that week (OR III-1 p.73, p.77). Men furnished: 12,357. State adjutant general: see st_adjutant_general_ohio. Capital: Columbus (OR III-1 p.73).

name: Governor of Oregon
sources: OR III-1 p.68; OR I-50 p.430; OR I-50 p.599
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: loyal. Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). No quota under the 15 Apr call (not among the 24 states, OR III-1 p.68). No item dated inside the window found in folder sources. Capital: addressed as Governor of Oregon, Salem (OR I-50 p.430).

name: Governor of Pennsylvania
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.76-77; OR III-1 p.82; OR III-1 p.256
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: loyal. Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 16 regiments plus 2 major-generals and 4 brigadier-generals (612 officers, 11,888 men, 12,500 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Philadelphia, Harrisburg. CONFLICT: the table's note says the quota was reduced by telegram of 16 Apr to 14 regiments (OR III-1 p.69); Cameron's letter to Curtin of 16 Apr says the requisition was modified 'so as to make it 14 instead of 10 regiments' (2 major-generals, 3 brigadier-generals, 14 colonels ... 8,900 privates) (OR III-1 p.77). Used: 16 per the table, cut to 14. Answer: complied. 16 Apr Secretary of the Commonwealth Eli Slifer: troops in Harrisburg within 24 hours, many unarmed (p.76-77); 17 Apr Curtin: volunteers arriving, many without arms, no ammunition, shall the Philadelphia regiments start (p.82). Men furnished: 20,175. No Pennsylvania adjutant general appears in the April correspondence (E. M. Biddle signs as adjutant general only on 5 Jun, OR III-1 p.256). Capital: Cameron addressed Curtin at Harrisburg (OR III-1 p.77).

name: Governor of Rhode Island
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.82; OR III-1 p.149
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: loyal. Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 1 regiment (37 officers, 743 men, 780 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Providence. Answer: complied, 17 Apr 1861 (a regiment already organized on Sprague's own offer to the President for the defence of the capital, about ready to move; one under the proclamation would follow if desired). Men furnished: 3,147. State adjutant general Mauran named 3 May (OR III-1 p.149). Capital: reply dated Providence (OR III-1 p.82); the state's second capital, Newport, is common knowledge.

name: Governor of South Carolina
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: confederate. Requisitions reach him from cs_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). No quota under the US call of 15 Apr: the proclamation names the state among those obstructing the laws and the call was not sent to it (OR III-1 p.67-68). CS requisitions: Walker's letter of 9 Mar counts 3,000 troops needed at Charleston, but the copies went only to AL, FL, GA, LA and MS (OR IV-1 p.135); 8 Apr: call to hold 3,000 volunteers drilled and ready (OR IV-1 p.211); 9 Apr: all infantry, or two artillery companies (OR IV-1 p.213). Answer: complied, 11 Apr 1861 (orders issued; one regiment of twelve companies to concentrate at Columbia, two more to hold ready) (OR I-1 p.304-305; cross-reference OR IV-1 p.219). 18 Apr: the further 5,000 'will be responded to' (OR IV-1 p.226). Capital: common knowledge (Columbia); Pickens worked from Charleston through the window (OR I-1 p.281, p.303-305).

name: Governor of Tennessee
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.81; OR IV-1 p.179-181
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: border (upper South). Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 2 regiments (74 officers, 1,486 men, 1,560 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Knoxville, Nashville. Answer: refused, 17 Apr 1861 ('will not furnish a single man for purpose of coercion, but 50,000, if necessary, for the defense of our rights') (OR III-1 p.81). Stance in the window: a Georgia commissioner (report, Savannah 20 Mar 1861; signature OCR unclear) found Harris deploring the February vote against a convention and holding union with the Confederacy 'only a question of time' (OR IV-1 p.179-181). Capital: 'Nashville, the capital' (OR IV-1 p.179).

name: Governor of Texas
notes: Sam Houston holds on 5 March (TX-CONV-1861 pp113-114). On 13 March Cave writes for Houston that he cannot recognize Confederate obligations (OR I-1 pp612-613). The Convention declares the offices vacant on 16 March and treats Lieutenant Governor Edward Clark as Governor that evening (TX-CONV-1861 pp183-187). R55's ungated succession notice proposes command.post_succession on 16 March; the named incumbent leaves the post without a status change. Confederate calls travel to this office; its department side does not establish Houston personally joined the Confederacy.

name: Governor of Vermont
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.73; OR III-1 p.75
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: loyal. Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 1 regiment (37 officers, 743 men, 780 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Burlington. Answer: complied, 15 Apr 1861 ('I shall promptly respond to your call for one regiment'). 16 Apr: rendezvous by 20 May suffices. Men furnished: 782. Capital: common knowledge (Montpelier); the governor telegraphed from Saint Johnsbury and the War Department addressed him there (OR III-1 p.73, p.75).

name: Governor of Virginia
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.76; OR IV-1 p.203-204; OR IV-1 p.221-223
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: border (upper South; the convention adopted secession on 17 Apr, outside the window, OR IV-1 p.223). Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 3 regiments (111 officers, 2,229 men, 2,340 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Staunton, Wheeling, Gordonsville. Answer: refused, 16 Apr 1861 ('the militia of Virginia will not be furnished to the powers at Washington'; doubted the telegram's genuineness) (OR III-1 p.76; cross-reference OR IV-1 p.222). Stance in the window: the General Assembly's joint resolution of 1 Apr 1861 records that the Assembly and the Governor had declared opposition to force against the seceded states and to troops marching through Virginia, and directs the Governor to seize the Bellona Foundry guns if moved (OR IV-1 p.203-204); 15 Apr the Governor and lieutenant-governor told a Confederate purchasing agent the guns were kept for Virginia's defence (OR IV-1 p.221). Men furnished: Virginia (western) 900. Capital: Executive Department, Richmond (OR III-1 p.76).

name: Governor of Wisconsin
sources: OR III-1 p.68-69 (15 Apr call, quota table, rendezvous, men furnished); OR III-1 p.72; OR III-1 p.75
notes: Alignment 15 Apr 1861: loyal. Requisitions reach him from us_secretary_war (state executive; no parent post). Quota under the 15 Apr 1861 call: 1 regiment (37 officers, 743 men, 780 aggregate). (Quota table OCR garbled; rows checked against its printed totals: 94 regiments, 3,549 officers, 69,842 men, 73,391 aggregate.) Rendezvous Milwaukee. 16 Apr: rendezvous by 20 May suffices. Answer: complied, 15 Apr 1861 ('will be promptly met, and further calls when made') (OR III-1 p.72). Men furnished: 817 (OCR 'S17'; the column total 91,816 confirms 817). Capital: Madison (OR III-1 p.72, p.75).

name: Forts Jackson and St. Philip (Louisiana troops)
notes: Seized by Louisiana 11 Jan 1861. A 'Major Duncan, Forts Jackson and St. Philip' was copied on Walker's telegram of 14 Mar. On 19 Mar Capt. J. M. Galt was sent to muster into C.S. service the 1,700 Louisiana troops called for (1,000 for Pensacola and 700 for the forts, 'including the number now serving in Forts Jackson and Saint Philip'); the number at the forts was to come from 'Brigadier-General Westmore' in New Orleans (name as printed). Van Dorn was ordered to these forts on 15 Mar, then sent to Texas instead. Side state: no evidence in these sources that the garrison was mustered into C.S. service by 15 Apr. [established: needs-source]

name: South Carolina Army (State regulars), commanding general
notes: State regular force. Beauregard reported on 8 Mar that the governor wanted the brigade of State Regulars kept as organised, under his orders, until it entered Confederate service. Walker (26 Mar) and Pickens (1 Apr) show the regulars had not been transferred and the State convention was to decide. Pickens: of 15 captains he appointed, 12 were ex-U.S. Army officers. Ripley's 1st Artillery Battalion had been under Dunovant since 2 Jan 1861. Staff (April): Maj. N. G. Evans, AG. Parent post id follows CONVENTIONS (governor post made by another agent). [established: needs-source]

name: Division of South Carolina Volunteers
notes: The volunteer companies raised under the act of 17 Dec 1860 were 104 companies, 8,835 rank and file in aggregate, forming ten regiments of ten companies in four brigades (Gist, S.C. Adjutant and Inspector General, 6 Mar 1861). This is statewide, not the strength at Charleston. Bonham, major-general, commanded; on 11 Apr three of its regiments were ordered into the field. [established: needs-source]

name: Adjutant and Inspector General and Chief of Ordnance, State of Texas (acting commander at San Antonio)
notes: P. N. Luckett (Texas Q.M. and Commissary General) wrote on 28 Mar that Colonel Maclin, 'adjutant and inspector general and chief of ordnance of the State', had been doing the duties of commanding officer at San Antonio, where the companies of two regiments (one State, one C.S.) were to gather. On 15 Apr Walker named 'Major Maclin, acting quartermaster' as a C.S. agent in Texas. [established: needs-source]

name: Commandant of Galveston (Texas Convention appointment)
notes: S. Sherman writes on 8 Mar that he was 'placed ... by the Convention commandant of Galveston'. [established: needs-source]

name: Committee of Public Safety, Texas Secession Convention
notes: A committee of the Convention, which directed the seizure of U.S. property. On 5 Feb 1861 it commissioned T. J. Devine, S. A. Maverick, P. N. Luckett and J. H. Rogers to demand Twiggs's surrender, the order citing Convention resolutions of 28 Jan 1861. The Convention adjourned 25 Mar 1861 (letter of 26 Mar). When the committee lapsed was not found. Not a governor's post, and it has no parent (the governor did not recognise the Convention). [established: needs-source] [abolished: needs-source]

name: Military Department of the Rio Grande (Texas State troops)
notes: Col. John S. Ford had been 'appointed commander of the Military Department of the Rio Grande' (commissioner E. B. Nichols, 23 Feb 1861). On 30 Mar H. E. McCulloch proposed leaving the Rio Grande, including El Paso, to 'Colonel Ford, of the State troops' and urged the C.S. to adopt the State regiment under Ford. Gov. Clark (4 Apr) asked the C.S. to accept the State's cavalry regiment. [established: needs-source]

name: Texas State troops, northwestern frontier
notes: H. E. McCulloch reported on 30 Mar that he had five companies under State authority on the northwestern frontier, three of which would be mustered into C.S. service. He had taken over from his brother Ben McCulloch the raising of the C.S. mounted rifle regiment. [established: needs-source]

name: Attorney General
notes: [source: the Senate Executive Journal, vol. XI, pp.289-290: the President's message of 5 March 1861 nominating the holder to this office (p.289; the Attorney General's on p.290), and the Senate's consent (p.290)]

name: District of Columbia militia (Inspector General)
sources: Cullum 1237; NOTE-march-1861-facts q.15 (NPS, Civil War Defenses of Washington, ch.4)
notes: Scott made Stone Inspector General of the District militia on 2 Jan 1861 (National Park Service via the research note). Cullum no. 1237 (2nd ed., 1879) gives Stone "Col. Staff, Inspector-General D. C. Volunteers, Jan. 1, 1861", in "Organizing and Disciplining District of Columbia Volunteers ... Jan. 1 to Apr. 16, 1861" and in command of them 16 Apr to 23 Jul 1861. The two sources differ by a day (1 or 2 Jan) and in the name of the force (volunteers or militia); the pack keeps the post as the militia's and the date as the start is empty.

name: Department of the East
notes: In existence at the start of the war; abolished 17 Aug 1861. Headquarters location needs-source.

name: Department of New Mexico
notes: Loring assumed command 22 March 1861. Dyer lists only the department created 9 Nov 1861.

name: Department of the Pacific
notes: Formed 15 Jan 1861 by merging the Departments of California and Oregon.

name: Department of Texas
notes: Twiggs surrendered the posts to Texas (16 Feb); Waite took command 19 Feb and was evacuating the troops by the coast through March and April; posts abandoned from 12 March to 13 April; officers at San Antonio seized 23 April (after the window).

name: Department of Utah
notes: Existence and commander in March 1861 needs-source (the Pacific department's limits exclude Utah east of the 117th meridian, OR I-50 p.1).

name: Department of the West
notes: Merged into the Western Department 3 July 1861.

name: Fort Jefferson
notes: Garrisoned 18 Jan 1861 from Fort Independence, Boston.

name: Fort Monroe
notes: Virginia had not seceded inside the window (convention voted 17 April). Supplied the men for Vogdes's company in January. Assignment to the Department of the East needs-source.

name: Fort Pickens
notes: Held under the truce of 28 Jan 1861. Vogdes landed and 'assumed command of the forces on the station' on 6 Feb but stayed aboard Brooklyn. Reinforced the night of 12 April; under the Department of Florida from 13 April.

name: Fort Sumter
notes: Garrison moved from Fort Moultrie 26 Dec 1860. Anderson wrote to the Adjutant General through the Charleston post office (2-3 days); inspected from 29 March, cut 8 April. Bombarded from 12 April, surrendered 13 April, evacuated 14 April 1861 (abolished date set to the surrender).

name: Fort Taylor and Key West Barracks
sources: OR I-1 pp.343, 351; OR I-1 chap. VII (instructions to the Texas transports)
notes: Garrisoned 14 Jan 1861. Two companies from the Texas evacuation were ordered landed at Key West barracks (instructions in OR I-1 chap. VII).

name: General-in-Chief (commanding the Army)
sources: Dyer p.254; OR I-1 p.599; NOTE-march-1861-facts design implication 8; FISHEL-CIA; NOTE-people-posts-1861
notes: Formally under the Secretary of War, but Lincoln gave Scott orders directly (verbal order of 5 March on Pickens, repeated in writing 11 March). Headquarters of the Army was still addressed at New York in March 1861 (OR I-1 p.599) though Scott was in Washington. Army commanders reported to the Adjutant General's office at Headquarters of the Army (OR I-1 p.599, Loring to Thomas, 23 Mar 1861). Filter role (0058): not set on this kind, because no source read shows Scott's headquarters holding, trimming or delaying a report in March 1861 (it relayed them, and Lincoln got Scott's opinion on them); the post is an [I] candidate only. Intelligence chief: none sourced for any Union post on 5 March 1861; Fishel says there was "no superior intelligence and counterintelligence agency at Washington" and that Pinkerton's bureau, attached to the Army of the Potomac, was at the capital for eight months of 1861-62 (FISHEL-CIA Part II), so intelligenceChief stays null.

name: Harpers Ferry Armory
sources: SEJ-XI p.34; SEJ-XI p.39; NPS-HAFE; NOTE-secession-winter-1861 s.1 (NPS)
notes: Burned by its small guard on 18 April 1861 (after the window). The Senate Executive Journal vol. XI prints the nomination of Alfred M. Barbour "to be superintendent of the United States armory at Harper's Ferry, Virginia" to date from 1 January 1859 (p.34, 13 Jan 1859) and his confirmation (p.39, 19 Jan 1859); the NPS names him superintendent in April 1861. Guard commander in the window: needs-source.

name: United States Marine Corps (Headquarters)
notes: NavyReg1861 p.99 lists Colonel John Harris, Commandant, with the Washington yard's Marine guard, plus Major Henry B. Tyler (adjutant and inspector) and Major William Russell (paymaster). Every yard had a Marine guard under a Marine officer (NavyReg1861 pp.98-100). The guards' strength in the window needs a source.

name: African Squadron
sources: ORN I-1 pp.xv-xvi, 24; SecNav1860 pp.233-234; SecNav1861 p.92
notes: 8 vessels in commission on 4 March, including the storeship Relief (ORN I-1). The flagship was the Constellation, though Inman had temporarily shifted his flag to the Portsmouth in spring 1861 (ORN I-1 p.24). SecNav1861 p.92 says the squadron was recalled except one vessel; the date of that order needs a source.

name: Brazil Squadron
sources: ORN I-1 pp.xv, 27, 30; SecNav1860 p.232; SecNav1861 p.92
notes: 3 ships in commission on 4 March (ORN I-1). The Seminole was ordered to Philadelphia on 8 April and the Congress home on 9 April; the orders arrived in May and June (ORN I-1 pp.27, 30). SecNav1861 p.92 says the squadron was recalled except one vessel. Inference: that vessel was the Pulaski, Sands's flag steamer in May (ORN I-1 p.27).

name: Bureau of Construction, Equipment and Repair
sources: Callahan pp.3-5; NavyReg1861 (Navy Department organization pages)
notes: The Engineer-in-Chief was attached to this bureau (NavyReg1861: Samuel Archbold). Callahan p.5 dates B. F. Isherwood as Engineer-in-Chief from 26 March 1861. That change falls inside the window but has no post of its own here. The 1842 date is the bureau's creation, outside the March–April 1861 window; it is kept as the post's origin.

name: Bureau of Medicine and Surgery
sources: Callahan pp.3-5; NavyReg1861 (Navy Department organization pages)
notes: Act of 31 August 1842 (Callahan p.3). The 1842 date is the bureau's creation, outside the March–April 1861 window; it is kept as the post's origin.

name: Bureau of Ordnance and Hydrography
sources: Callahan pp.3-5; NavyReg1861 (Navy Department organization pages)
notes: Conflict over who was chief: the NavyReg1861 department page prints D. N. Ingraham as chief, but its captains' list gives G. A. Magruder 'Chief Bureau of Ordnance, &c.' Callahan p.4 resolves it: Ingraham 10 Mar 1856 to 23 Sep 1860, Magruder 24 Sep 1860 to 23 Apr 1861, A. A. Harwood from 24 Apr 1861. The department page was stale. The 1842 date is the bureau's creation, outside the March–April 1861 window; it is kept as the post's origin.

name: Bureau of Provisions and Clothing
sources: Callahan pp.3-5; NavyReg1861 (Navy Department organization pages)
notes: Act of 31 August 1842 (Callahan p.3). The 1842 date is the bureau's creation, outside the March–April 1861 window; it is kept as the post's origin.

name: Bureau of Navy Yards and Docks
sources: Callahan pp.3-5; NavyReg1861 (Navy Department organization pages)
notes: One of the five bureaus set up by the Act of 31 August 1842 (Callahan p.3). It did not command the yards: commandants reported to the Secretary. The 1842 date is the bureau's creation, outside the March–April 1861 window; it is kept as the post's origin.

name: East India Squadron
sources: ORN I-1 p.xv; SecNav1860 pp.235-237; SecNav1861 p.92
notes: 5 vessels in commission on 4 March. The ORN I-1 list also puts the Niagara (special service, homeward from Japan) under this heading. Recalled (SecNav1861 p.92); the date of the order needs a source.

name: Home Squadron
notes: SecNav1861: on 4 March the squadron had 12 vessels, 187 guns and about 2,000 men; only 4 small vessels (25 guns, about 280 men) were in northern ports. The ORN I-1 list of 4 March names the 12 ships. Their guns sum to 187, and the 4 at New York or Washington (Pawnee, Crusader, Mohawk, Supply) carry 25 guns and 292 crew. On 2 Feb Toucey recalled the Powhatan, Pocahontas and Cumberland from Vera Cruz (ORN I-4 p.76). On 5 April the Powhatan, Pawnee and Pocahontas were 'withdrawn temporarily' for special service (ORN I-4 p.234). On 10 April Pendergrast asked for a steam flagship (p.268). On 16 April the Cumberland's return to Vera Cruz was deferred (p.278). Renamed West India squadron later in 1861 (SecNav1861 p.92), outside the window.

name: Mediterranean Squadron
notes: 3 ships in commission on 4 March (ORN I-1). Recalled by Department letters of 8 and 11 April 1861: the Susquehanna and Iroquois to go to New York, then the Richmond. Bell received the letters on 4 May (ORN I-1 p.20). The storeship Release, which NavyReg1861 lists with this squadron on 1 Jan 1861, was at New York by 27 March (see her force block).

name: Pacific Squadron
sources: ORN I-1 pp.xvi, 15; SecNav1860 pp.234-235; SecNav1861 pp.85, 91-92, 96-97; NavyReg1861 p.96
notes: 7 vessels on the 4 March list. One is the Levant, which sailed from Hilo on 18 Sept 1860 and was given up as lost (SecNav1861 pp.91, 96-97). The squadron was not recalled. On 27 April Welles ordered it to concentrate on the Panama to San Francisco route (ORN I-1 p.15). The storeships Warren (Panama) and Fredonia (Valparaiso) were permanent stationary storeships and are not counted (NavyReg1861 p.96; SecNav1861 p.85). SecNav1861 p.92 (July) gives the squadron as 6 vessels, 82 guns and 1,000 men.

name: Boston Navy Yard
notes: Commandant confirmed as Hudson on 27 April 1861 (ORN I-1 p.15).

name: Mare Island Navy Yard
sources: NavyReg1861 p.100; Callahan p.143; OR I-50 p.481
notes: NavyReg1861 heads it 'San Francisco, Cal.' Commandant R. B. Cunningham died on 13 March 1861 (Callahan p.143). Commander D. McDougal, listed second at the yard (NavyReg1861 p.100), was commandant by 9 May (OR I-50 p.481). When he took over needs a source.

name: New York Navy Yard
notes: The receiving ship North Carolina lay here under Commander James H. Ward (NavyReg1861 p.99). The yard fitted out the Powhatan and the Sumter and Pickens ships in April. Commander A. H. Foote signed as acting or 'pro' commandant while Breese was away on court-martial duty in Washington (ORN I-4 p.91).

name: Norfolk Navy Yard (Gosport)
notes: In ordinary there on 1 Jan 1861: Pennsylvania (receiving ship), Columbus, Delaware, United States, Columbia, Raritan, Plymouth, Germantown, Dolphin and the steam frigate Merrimack, with the New York on the stocks (NavyReg1861 pp.95-96). On 11 March the Germantown was due to be ready for a crew by 25 March (ORN I-4 p.272). Orders of 10, 11, 12 and 16 April told the yard to make the Merrimack, Plymouth, Dolphin and Germantown ready to move (ORN I-4 pp.274-278; SecNav1861 pp.86-87). The yard was abandoned and burned on 20-21 April, after the window.

name: Philadelphia Navy Yard
sources: NavyReg1861 p.99; ORN I-4 pp.106, 139; ORN I-1 p.15
notes: Put the Water Witch in commission on 10 April 1861 (ORN I-4 p.106).

name: Portsmouth Navy Yard
notes: NavyReg1861 heads it 'Portsmouth, N. H.' Commandant confirmed as Pearson on 27 April 1861 (ORN I-1 p.15).

name: Sackett's Harbor naval station
notes: Not a yard. NavyReg1861 p.100 lists only ships 'in ordinary' (Captain Josiah Tattnall, Commander Thomas R. Rootes, Lieutenant Thomas Pattison) and a recruiting rendezvous. The ship of the line New Orleans was on the stocks here (p.95). Tattnall resigned on 21 Feb 1861 (Callahan p.634, spelled Tatnall). The holder on 4 March needs a source. Rootes was dismissed on 19 April 1861 (Callahan p.473).

name: Washington Navy Yard
sources: NavyReg1861 pp.97, 99; SecNav1861 p.94; ORN I-4 pp.228-229, 240
notes: Also the Marine Corps headquarters and the Navy's ordnance works (SecNav1861 p.94). The steam tender Anacostia was 'in service' here (NavyReg1861 p.97).

name: Postmaster General
notes: Blair was Fox's brother-in-law and the cabinet's strongest voice for relieving Sumter (research notes).[source: the Senate Executive Journal, vol. XI, pp.289-290: the President's message of 5 March 1861 nominating the holder to this office (p.289; the Attorney General's on p.290), and the Senate's consent (p.290)]

name: President of the United States
notes: Commander in chief (Dyer p.254). Inauguration 4 March 1861.

name: Private Secretary to the President
notes: A caller-screening post, with role null on purpose (lead's ruling, 2026-11-15): in the kernel a role-filter post sits on the wire and every telegraph report passes it first, and 0040 leaves the March 1861 telegraph filter empty; screening callers and mail is a Phase 1 filter on informal routes. The Executive Journal records the President's messages of 5 March 1861 as received "by Mr. Nicolay, his secretary" (SEJ-XI p.289), and the New York Times's Washington dispatch of 7 March reports that at the White House "all callers have first to see Nicolay, the Secretary, who now bears the brunt of the labor" (NYT-1861-03-08). What he screened is callers: that he also sorted the mail, or held telegrams, is not sourced. Not Senate-confirmed; there is no commission date.

name: Revenue Marine (Revenue Cutter Service)
notes: Treasury's armed cutters. Head of the service in March 1861: needs-source. Tried 2026-11-15: a search summary says the Revenue Marine Bureau (chief Alexander V. Fraser, 1843-49) was dissolved in 1849 and the service ran under another Treasury office until 1869-71 (snippet, unchecked); the Coast Guard history site and its chronology PDF refused automated fetches and were not routed around; so neither the post's form nor its head is sourced. Kept as a post, marked needs-source: a snippet may not remove a post (L13), as it may not add one (lead's ruling, 2026-11-15).

name: Secretary of the Interior
notes: Vacant under Buchanan after Jacob Thompson's resignation (January 1861): needs-source; no nomination to the office appears in the Executive Journal for January-March 1861 (read, not conclusive). The Senate Executive Journal vol. XI, p.289 prints the President's message of 5 March 1861 nominating Caleb B. Smith "to be Secretary of the Interior".

name: Secretary of the Navy
sources: Callahan p.1; NavyReg1861 (Navy Department organization pages)
notes: Toucey held it to 7 March 1861; Welles appointed 7 March 1861 (Callahan p.1). Navy yards and squadrons report directly to the Secretary. Chief Clerk under Toucey: Charles W. Welsh (NavyReg1861). Tenure columns in people_in_posts use the Senate confirmation date, 5 March 1861, for every Lincoln cabinet member; Callahan's 7 March is kept here as the appointment date (see welles_gideon).
